rows.note: Use this all-purpose colloquial adverb for “still/yet”; in negative clauses it commonly combines with 未, and it also covers remaining time and “even more.”

example.jyutping: nei5 zung6 mei6 sik6 faan6 aa3

rows.note: Use this plain negative adverb for “not yet,” especially when the added sense of “still” is unnecessary.

example.english: I haven't seen that movie yet.
example.jyutping: ngo5 mei6 tai2 go2 tou3 hei3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for contrasting one clause with another.

example.english: I want to go, yet it’s raining today.
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 heoi3 daan6 hai6 gam1 jat6 lok6 jyu5

rows.note: Use this especially for sentence-initial “however” or to introduce a qualification after stating something.

example.english: This restaurant is pretty good, yet it’s a bit expensive.
example.traditional: 呢間餐廳幾好食，不過價錢貴咗啲。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 gei2 hou2 sik6 bat1 gwo3 gaa3 cin2 gwai3 zo2 di1

rows.note: Use this for the future-looking sense that something will eventually happen, rather than for present or remaining situations.

example.jyutping: nei5 zung2 wui5 ming4 baak6 ge3
